name: mr_save_request
description: Saves a confirmed material request as a child entity of the requestor's site and notifies the approver. Validates the collected fields before writing; on validation failure it messages the requestor with the exact problem and returns success:false so the flow stays on the previous step (calling step should use successMode 'lenient'). stateParams always carries: requestEntityId, requestNumber, approverPhone (empty strings on failure). success:true means the record was written; the approver notify is best-effort and never fails the step.

siteEntityId.description: Entity id of the requestor's site (parent record), bound from state

materialName.description: Material name collected earlier in the flow

quantity.description: Quantity the requestor typed, as raw text — validated here

requestorName.description: Requestor's display name from system context

workflowDefinition.description: Parse and validate the collected request, look up the site for its approver, create the material-request entity under the site, then notify the approver only when one is configured.

nodes.name: Parse input and validate quantity
Save only when the quantity is valid

trueBranch.name: Check the lookup envelope and read the approver
Create the material request under the site
Check the create envelope
Only announce a request that was actually saved
Build the confirmation text
Tell the requestor the request is in
Notify the approver only when one is configured

falseBranch.name: Tell the requestor the save failed
Tell the requestor what was wrong

nodes.name: Build the result the engine reads

__annotations.why_this_example_exists: Demonstrates the mandatory disciplines the SKILL.md describes: (1) validate BEFORE writing — the create_entity node lives inside the validation's trueBranch; (2) every platform result is envelope-checked in a code node before its fields are used (read_site, check_create); (3) the child entity carries parentId and flowTrackingId; (4) nothing announces success until check_create confirms the write landed — saved_guard wraps the confirmation and the notify, and its falseBranch tells the requestor instead of leaving them with a success message for a record that does not exist; (5) the third-party notify is wrapped in a further if-else on `exists` (false for empty string) so a site with no approver never crashes or messages nobody; (6) the result node is FLAT — success, message, stateParams, and no top-level `data`/`result`/`type` key that would make normalizeToolResult unwrap it and discard stateParams; (7) it returns the SAME stateParams keys on every path, chooses success deliberately, and sends the failure message from inside the tool because the engine sends nothing on failure; (8) isIdempotent true only on read/parse code nodes — the writes and sends are tool nodes and are never retried; (9) every send in this graph — confirmation, save-failure, invalid-input — goes through send_template_message, including the fully computed confirmation text, which uses a single-placeholder template (mr_save_request__confirm_to_requestor, body "{{TEXT}}") instead of a free-text send; (10) none of those three templates has a spec action behind it, so none exists in generatedTemplates — this tool's own additionalTemplates.json output mints all three, shown in references/mr_additional_templates.json.
__annotations.whole_string_reference_note: confirm_to_requestor's TEXT parameter is '$build_confirmation.text' — a reference must be the ENTIRE string, so 'Request $x saved' would be sent as that literal. Any composite text is assembled in a code node (build_confirmation) and referenced as one whole value, passed as the template's single placeholder parameter — templates do not require a fixed skeleton in the spec's text, a template can be just "{{TEXT}}". An unresolvable reference does not throw: it becomes undefined, and send_template_message reports it back as an "Error: …" string rather than throwing — check for that string, not an envelope.
__annotations.branch_reference_note: build_final_response references check_create and read_site, which only run in the trueBranch. That is safe ONLY because the code first checks parsed.isValid and returns before touching them on the false path — a $() call for a node that did not run returns {}, so guard before you read. Never reference a branching node itself (saved_guard, notify_guard): $() unwraps only tool and code nodes.
